title: Promoting the Negative Pell Squaring Bridge into Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁
description: Answers the parent's open question: promotes the scalar squaring identity (x²+2y²)²−2(2xy)²=1 into Mathlib's group-theoretic Pell model. Given norm −1 solutions of x²−2y²=−1, their ℤ√2 product lands in Pell.Solution₁ 2 (the norm +1 group), and the squaring bridge is exactly the diagonal of that product — with the promoted value literally the square ⟨x,y⟩² inside ℤ√2. A coset-closure lemma shows the norm −1 solutions form the 'other half' of the unit group of ℤ√2. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.

meta.author: Lean Genius (promotion into Pell.Solution₁); Brahmagupta (norm composition)
originalContributions: negMul_norm: Brahmagupta's identity specialized to d=2 — the product of two norm −1 solutions of x²−2y²=−1 satisfies the norm +1 Pell equation, (x₁x₂+2y₁y₂)²−2(x₁y₂+y₁x₂)²=1, proved by a single ring rewrite plus (−1)·(−1)=1
negMul: promotion of that product into Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ 2 via Solution₁.mk, turning a pair of scalar negative-Pell solutions into a genuine element of the positive Pell solution group
coe_negMul: the promoted element's underlying ℤ√2 value is literally the honest product ⟨x₁,y₁⟩·⟨x₂,y₂⟩, connecting the ad-hoc coordinate formulas to Zsqrtd multiplication (re_mul/im_mul)
negSquare: the squaring bridge itself, valued in Pell.Solution₁ 2 — the diagonal negMul x y x y, sending a single norm −1 solution (x,y) to the positive solution (x²+2y², 2xy)
coe_negSquare: the promoted square equals ⟨x,y⟩² in ℤ√2, giving the precise sense in which the parent's scalar identity negPell_sq_is_pos_pell IS squaring inside Mathlib's Pell model
negSquare_one_one: the fundamental negative solution (1,1) squares to the fundamental positive Pell solution (3,2) of Pell.Solution₁ 2

posMul_neg_norm: COSET CLOSURE — multiplying a positive Pell solution a ∈ Solution₁ 2 by a negative solution stays in the negative coset (norm (+1)·(−1)=−1), witnessing that the norm −1 solutions are exactly 'half' of the unit group of ℤ√2
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-checked: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. Self-contained — imports only Mathlib.NumberTheory.Pell (for Pell.Solution₁ and the Zsqrtd ℤ√d API) and Mathlib.Tactic; does not depend on the parent proof file.

crossReferences.description: Parent entry: classifies the positive-integer solutions of x²−2y²=−1 and proves the scalar squaring identity negPell_sq_is_pos_pell. Its second open question — 'promote the squaring bridge into Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ type, exhibiting the negative Pell chain as the half of the positive Pell unit group of norm −1 elements' — is exactly what this entry answers.
The classical (norm +1) Pell equation x² − Dy² = 1, modelled by Mathlib as Pell.Solution₁. This entry realizes the negative-Pell chain inside that group via the multiplicative structure of ℤ√2.

overview.historicalContext: Brahmagupta's identity (628 CE) — the composition law (a²−Nb²)(c²−Nd²)=(ac+Nbd)²−N(ad+bc)² — is the multiplicativity of the norm form of ℤ[√N]. It underlies the entire modern theory of the Pell equation: solutions of x²−Dy²=1 form a group isomorphic to the units of norm +1 of ℤ[√D]. When the negative Pell equation x²−Dy²=−1 is solvable (for D=2 it is, √2 having odd continued-fraction period), the norm ±1 units together form the full unit group, with the norm −1 units a single coset of the norm +1 subgroup — the fundamental unit 1+√2 of ℤ[√2] has norm −1, and its square 3+2√2 generates the norm +1 solutions. Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ formalizes only the norm +1 group; this entry connects the parent's elementary treatment of the norm −1 case to that machinery through Brahmagupta composition.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry proves the scalar identity (x²+2y²)²−2(2xy)²=1 for any solution of x²−2y²=−1, but this identity lives entirely in ℤ and never touches Mathlib's group model Pell.Solution₁. Can the squaring bridge be promoted into Pell.Solution₁ 2, exhibiting the negative-Pell solutions as the 'half' (the norm −1 coset) of the unit group of ℤ√2?
overview.proofStrategy: Work through the norm form of ℤ√2. Brahmagupta's identity (negMul_norm) shows a product of two norm −1 solutions is a norm +1 solution; Solution₁.mk promotes it to Pell.Solution₁ 2 (negMul). The lemma coe_negMul identifies the promoted element's underlying ℤ√2 value with the honest Zsqrtd product ⟨x₁,y₁⟩·⟨x₂,y₂⟩ (via re_mul/im_mul), so the promotion is not an ad-hoc coordinate formula but genuine multiplication in the ring. The squaring bridge (negSquare) is the diagonal negMul x y x y, and coe_negSquare identifies it with ⟨x,y⟩². Finally posMul_neg_norm shows the norm −1 solutions are closed under the Solution₁ 2-action, exhibiting them as a single coset — the 'other half' of the unit group.
keyInsights: The promotion is fundamentally about ℤ√2 multiplication, not coordinate bookkeeping: coe_negMul proves the promoted Solution₁ element equals the literal Zsqrtd product ⟨x₁,y₁⟩·⟨x₂,y₂⟩, so the whole construction is 'multiply in the ring, read off that the norm is +1'.

The squaring bridge is a special case of a two-argument composition law. Framing it as the diagonal negSquare = negMul x y x y makes transparent why squaring works — it is (−1)·(−1)=+1 — and simultaneously yields the coset structure.

Coset closure (posMul_neg_norm) is the structural heart of 'the negatives are half the unit group': the norm +1 solutions are a subgroup and the norm −1 solutions are the unique nontrivial coset, since (+1)·(−1)=−1 keeps you in the negative class while (−1)·(−1)=+1 returns you to the subgroup.

Everything reduces to norm-multiplicativity, so every proof is a single ring/linear identity plus a sign computation — no descent, no induction, no decidability. The content is the *bridge* to Mathlib's API, made honest by the coe_ lemmas.
Concretely the fundamental unit 1+√2 (the pair (1,1), norm −1) squares to 3+2√2 (the pair (3,2), the fundamental Pell solution): negSquare_one_one records this inside Pell.Solution₁ 2.

sections.title: Module Header and Coset Framing
sections.summary: Explains that the parent's squaring identity is purely scalar and states the goal: promote it into Pell.Solution₁ 2 by exhibiting the norm −1 solutions as a coset of the norm +1 unit group of ℤ√2.
sections.mathContext: The unit group of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt2]$ (mod $\pm1$) is generated by $1+\sqrt2$ of norm $-1$; the norm $+1$ solutions (Mathlib's $\texttt{Pell.Solution}_1\,2$) are its index-2 subgroup, with the norm $-1$ solutions the nontrivial coset.

sections.title: Brahmagupta composition and promotion
sections.summary: negMul_norm proves the product of two norm −1 solutions is a norm +1 solution; negMul promotes it into Pell.Solution₁ 2; coe_negMul identifies the promoted value with the literal ℤ√2 product.
sections.mathContext: Brahmagupta's identity for $d=2$: $(x_1x_2+2y_1y_2)^2-2(x_1y_2+y_1x_2)^2=(x_1^2-2y_1^2)(x_2^2-2y_2^2)=(-1)(-1)=1$. In $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt2]$ this is $\langle x_1,y_1\rangle\cdot\langle x_2,y_2\rangle$.

sections.title: The squaring bridge, promoted
sections.summary: negSquare is the diagonal of negMul, mapping a norm −1 solution to (x²+2y², 2xy) ∈ Pell.Solution₁ 2; coe_negSquare identifies it with ⟨x,y⟩²; negSquare_one_one records that (1,1) squares to the fundamental Pell solution (3,2).
sections.mathContext: $\langle x,y\rangle^2=\langle x^2+2y^2,\,2xy\rangle$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt2]$; $(1+\sqrt2)^2=3+2\sqrt2$, so $(1,1)\mapsto(3,2)$, the fundamental solution of $x^2-2y^2=1$.

sections.title: Coset closure
sections.summary: posMul_neg_norm shows multiplying a positive Pell solution by a negative solution yields another negative solution, exhibiting the norm −1 solutions as a single coset — the 'other half' of the unit group. A numeric example checks (7,5) squares to (99,70).
sections.mathContext: Norm is a homomorphism $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt2]^\times\to\{\pm1\}$; the norm $+1$ solutions are its kernel and the norm $-1$ solutions the nontrivial coset, closed under multiplication by $\texttt{Solution}_1\,2$.

conclusion.summary: This fully verified 142-line file (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) answers the parent's second open question by promoting the negative-Pell squaring bridge into Mathlib's group-theoretic Pell model. Brahmagupta composition (negMul_norm) sends products of norm −1 solutions into Pell.Solution₁ 2 (negMul), the promotion is identified with honest ℤ√2 multiplication (coe_negMul, coe_negSquare), the squaring bridge is realized as the diagonal (negSquare), and coset closure (posMul_neg_norm) exhibits the norm −1 solutions as the 'other half' of the unit group of ℤ√2.
conclusion.implications: The entry closes the gap between the parent's elementary, scalar treatment of x²−2y²=−1 and Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ API. The pattern — realize an ad-hoc coordinate identity as multiplication in the appropriate ring, then read off norm behavior — is reusable for any norm-form Diophantine problem where Mathlib provides only the norm +1 solution group.
openQuestions: Package negMul and posMul_neg_norm as an honest coset structure: define the type of norm −1 solutions and prove it is a torsor for Pell.Solution₁ 2, with the full unit group of ℤ√2 (mod ±1) recovered as the disjoint union of the two classes.

Prove the squaring map from norm −1 solutions is a bijection onto the odd powers of the fundamental Pell unit, upgrading the numeric checks (1,1)↦(3,2), (7,5)↦(99,70) to a structural statement about powers of 3+2√2.
